title: Use the magnetic meter
html:
Look for clues to concealed electronics. Some electronic components produce magnetic fields that your iPhone’s magnetometer may detect at close range—even without a recognizable wireless broadcast. Use the magnetic meter in Area Sweep during a careful physical inspection of accessible places you are allowed to inspect.

Use repeatable changes to decide where to take a closer physical look, not as proof of a hidden device. It cannot identify a device, measure its distance, reveal its intent, or prove that it is recording.

Ordinary speakers, magnets, wiring, chargers, magnetic metal, and phone accessories can all affect readings. Some cameras, microphones, and other electronics produce little measurable change. No change is not an all-clear.

Aim the sensor, not the whole phone

The sensor occupies one small point and its position varies by model. On iPhone 17 Pro Max, Apple's dimensional drawing places the compass in the lower-back area near the USB-C end—not the camera area. Do not apply this location to every iPhone. A sensor-location check with a familiar object is more useful than assuming the camera or contactless-payment area is the correct point.

Practice before a sweep

  1. In Guide, open Reading the magnetic meter, choose Practice with the magnetometer, then tap Start Practice. Practice is also available before a magnetic Area Sweep.
  2. Compare an ordinary speaker you own with a spot away from electronics. Remove magnetic accessories if practical.
  3. Keep a gap. Move slowly over the same spot, holding the angle and distance consistent. Never press strong magnets against the phone or open equipment.
  4. Watch Actual Field and Δ Reference. Repeat the pass and learn which phone positions produce a repeatable response; do not aim for a particular number.

Practice does not collect Bluetooth or local-network findings, create exports, or save a session. Stop Practice, Done, or leaving the app clears the readings. Returning does not resume measurement; tap Start Practice when ready. Practice is familiarization, not calibration or a pass/fail hardware test.

Use magnetic measurements in an Area Sweep

  1. On Scan, choose Area Sweep, select Motion and magnetic, and tap Continue. Bluetooth and local-network discovery are separate choices; you can use magnetic measurements on their own.
  2. Follow the preparation and access guidance, then tap Begin Area Sweep. Keep Spectra visible and your iPhone unlocked. Pause away from obvious magnets or electronics so a stable display reference can form.
  3. Move slowly through accessible areas you are allowed to inspect. Keep the sensor position, angle, and gap consistent. Watch Actual Field or Δ Reference, then repeat any noticeable change over the same spot. A change is a clue, not an identified device.
  4. Choose Finish Area Sweep when ready. Review Coverage, the magnetic events, and Review graph when graph data is available. Check the saved status before closing. Automatic saving follows your Save completed sessions preference. With automatic saving off, choose Save Session to keep just this check without changing your preference.

Area Sweep initially allows 30 minutes. A notice five minutes before the deadline lets you extend or finish; if you do nothing, collection ends at the deadline. This does not enable background measurement or remove graph-retention limits.

Understand the numbers

  • Actual Field shows the measured field in microteslas (µT). The reading card is labeled Actual field.
  • Δ Reference shows the signed difference from your display reference. Its reading card is labeled Delta from reference. A larger magnitude means a larger field change, not proven proximity.
  • Rebuild Reference chooses a fresh display comparison. It does not reset the independent event detector or erase recorded events.

Why a visible change may not become an event

Automatic spike detection uses calibrated samples, a noise-adaptive threshold, persistence, and strong-spike rules. Small fluctuations or poor-quality measurements may not qualify. If calibration is limited, the actual-field trace can continue without automatic spike marking. Check Measurement Details; stale or unavailable readings are not a quiet field.

Completed magnetic sweeps can include Review graph, a bounded, downsampled history—not every measurement. Earlier readings may be omitted in long sweeps. A saved graph shows past measurements; it does not resume collection.

Keep the limits in view

Inspect safely and respect other people's privacy. Do not tamper with equipment or confront someone based on a magnetic change. A flat response does not rule out a device and is not a pass/fail test of your phone. Magnetic measurements are one source of context, not a hidden-camera detector or a safety certification.

For the complete measurement workflow, see the Spectra Guide. For missing or unexpected readings, see Troubleshoot missing devices and unexpected readings.

title: Understand Monitor and its baseline
html:
Monitor compares radio observations with a baseline while your iPhone stays in one place. It is not an unattended security alarm or a count of people arriving and leaving.

This article describes the 1.1.0 release candidate. The public App Store version is 1.0.0; its older dashboard does not include the recorded-count and activity-snapshot controls below.

Establish the starting comparison

  1. Choose Monitor, select the radio measurements you need, and keep the iPhone stationary.
  2. Keep Spectra visible and the phone unlocked. Each available source needs 30 seconds of active observation; permission waiting does not count.
  3. If useful, choose Add 30 seconds to baseline once to extend the comparison to 60 seconds per source.

The starting baseline begins automatically, and the countdown follows the slowest participating source. When it is ready, New identities recorded starts at zero and the panel shows its capture time and elapsed comparison time. No duration guarantees discovery of every device. Baseline findings remain in the retained inventory: initially observed does not mean trusted.

Read changes without overinterpreting them

New identities recorded counts signal-identity lineages first observed after this baseline, excluding identities seen earlier in the same Monitor session. A known identity does not become new after a fresh baseline, a quiet period, or inventory eviction. This is a recorded comparison count across all Monitor measurements, regardless of result filters—not a count of physical devices or currently present signals.

The recorded count is independent of the latest 40 retained events. Older activity or inventory rows leaving their bounded history do not reduce it, but later evidence or an explicit discovery-identity replacement can correct it. Incomplete history or a recording limit is disclosed; uncertain identities are not invented as new. Older or imported reports without a recorded count show Unavailable, not zero.

Open View activity & help to review timestamped retained activity while Monitor continues. The view is a fixed snapshot: close and reopen it for later activity. It retains up to 40 raw events, including baseline capture when present; repeated identity-and-kind events are combined for reading. The recorded count can exceed the identities and activity still available for inspection.

  • Newly observed identity: an identity recorded as new for this comparison, not necessarily a newly arrived device.
  • Signal returned: an already-known identity was observed again. This is a historical event, not proof a physical device left, returned, or is still present.
  • Not recently observed: a previously observed identity stopped being observed. Earlier dashboards called this Not recently seen. For Bluetooth, the wait is 45 seconds; local-network services follow Bonjour announcements and removals.

Sleep, identity rotation, interference, and broadcast behavior can produce changes without physical movement. One identity can have several kinds of activity; the timeline is not a current missing-device total or unlimited lifetime history.

Acknowledge or restart intentionally

Mark changes reviewed acknowledges the latest displayed change without resetting the recorded count, trusting a device, erasing evidence, or changing the baseline. Opening activity or the Guide does not acknowledge changes or stop measurement.

For a fresh reference, tap New Baseline in the main Monitor panel. The tap starts a new 30-second observation window immediately. When it is ready, the new comparison's recorded count begins at zero, but identities seen earlier in the same Monitor session remain known. Earlier comparisons, their recorded counts when available, and retained events stay in the session after Stop Monitor. Wait for the current baseline to finish before starting another; up to nine comparisons fit in one session. Stop and start another Monitor when that limit is reached. Spectra does not automatically judge that you moved or replace the baseline for you.

Finish and review coverage

Choose Stop Monitor for the full retained inventory and detailed results; it is not required to read the activity snapshot. The inventory distinguishes Since baseline, Starting baseline, and Earlier observations retained from before the current comparison. These sections describe observation time, not trusted or untrusted devices.

Switching apps or locking the iPhone ends measurement. Review Coverage for source loss and interruptions. A late or recovering source gets its own 30-second observation window; recovery alone does not make an already-known identity new or rewrite the original baseline. Partial local-network coverage can keep novelty uncertain until full recovery and warm-up.

Radio intensity is not a measure of risk, and a quiet dashboard is not an all-clear. See the Spectra Guide for complete baseline and retention details.

title: Use Spectra while traveling and in shared spaces
html:
Use Spectra to inform your next decision—not to certify that a space is safe. Silent, wired, shielded, powered-off, or unrecognizable devices can remain invisible.

Hotels, rentals, and shared housing

Start with a Quick Check to get oriented. Use an unhurried Area Sweep for accessible areas you are allowed to inspect. In gyms and changing rooms, respect other people's privacy and facility rules. A broadcast may come from outside the room; an unfamiliar name is not evidence of covert recording.

For a close-range physical inspection, select Motion and magnetic in Area Sweep. Repeatable changes may warrant a closer look for concealed electronics, even without a recognizable wireless broadcast. Ordinary magnets and magnetic metal can cause changes too; no change does not rule out a device. See Use the magnetic meter for safe practice and the limits.

Rideshares, cafés, and travel hubs

As a passenger or while waiting, a Quick Check offers a short snapshot. Specialist checks focus on supported glasses or wearable matches. Crowds contain ordinary devices, and a name or signal strength cannot identify the person carrying one. Do not scan while driving or confront someone based on a result.

Review what the check actually covered

Inspect Coverage, clear measurement filters and name search, and consider unclassified activity. In specialist checks, View observed activity offers wider context. Expected is your label for the check, not authenticated safety. A saved check describes an earlier observation, not the space now.

Protect your connection, too

Confirm the intended Wi-Fi name with the venue through a trusted channel. A familiar network name alone does not authenticate it. Prefer cellular data when you do not trust the connection, keep software updated, protect accounts with multifactor authentication, and heed certificate warnings.

A reputable VPN can protect traffic routed through its tunnel between your phone and the VPN service; trust shifts to that provider. It does not prevent nearby recording, authenticate a hotspot, make a malicious website safe, or make you anonymous. Follow your organization's policy. VPN settings may affect local discovery; do not disable required protection or join an unfamiliar network just to find more devices. Spectra does not provide a VPN.

Keep useful context without collecting unnecessary personal details

Rename a saved session and add notes about repeatable observations, areas inspected, ordinary explanations, and unresolved questions. Notes are yours, not sensor evidence. Avoid sensitive itinerary or personal details, and review reports before sharing. Local-network browsing can send queries visible to others on that network; it is not covert.

For a credible threat or highly sensitive activity, move sensitive conversations to a more appropriate location and consult a trusted security contact. Do not tamper with equipment based on an app result.

Read the full Guide and privacy policy.

title: Contact Arc Signal support
html:
Need help with Spectra? Email support@arcsignal.dev. Please do not send passwords, account recovery codes, or payment-card details.

Include the essentials

  • What you tried, what you expected, and what happened instead.
  • The check type, selected measurements, and exact error message.
  • In iPhone Spectra, choose Settings → Support information → Copy support information for app, engine, catalog, hardware, and OS context. Review it before copying and sending; it does not attach scan data.
  • For the Experimental Watch companion, include its Settings → About version, release, and build, plus whether the display dimmed or the sweep ended early.

Share only what is needed

Scan archives can include broadcast names, identifiers, network information, raw payloads, and personal notes. Start without an archive. If one is needed to investigate a problem, review the export and share it deliberately. Reduced identifying information is not anonymous. Location tags are excluded from exports by default. A single report uses Include scan location; Export All Sessions uses Include scan locations; Export Selected uses the same collection control. Leave these off for support unless the location itself is necessary. For a scan issue, share only the relevant session rather than a whole collection. Reduced identifying information can include location too if you explicitly choose it. Check screenshots for personal or location details.

Nothing is sent to support automatically. Google Workspace handles support email; Zoho Desk handles support tickets and replies.

Useful links

  • Arc Signal website
  • Complete Spectra Guide
  • Spectra privacy policy

Company and product information is also available in Spectra through Settings → About Spectra → Arc Signal website.

Support can help explain an app issue, but cannot certify a location as safe or provide an emergency response. For an immediate safety concern, use appropriate local assistance.
